title: Ibn Battuta: Central Asia and the road to Delhi, 1332–34
summary: From the Volga across the desert to Khwarizm and Bukhara, a winter with the Chagatai khan, over the Oxus to Balkh, round Khorasan, over the Hindu Kush to Kabul, and down to the Indus and Delhi.

events.label: Bukhara in ruins
events.text: Most of Bukhara's mosques, colleges and bazaars still lay in ruins from the Mongol sack a century before.

events.label: The camp of Tarmashirin
events.text: He stayed fifty-four days at the camp of Tarmashirin, the first Chagatai khan of Transoxiana to take up Islam.

events.label: The Hindu Kush
events.text: He waited for warm weather to cross it, and gives the name as 'the slayer of the Indians', because so many of the enslaved boys and girls brought from India died there of cold and snow.

events.label: The Indus, on 1 Muharram 734
events.text: The Rihla says he came to the Indus on the first day of the year 734, 12 September 1333. It is the one firm date the chronology of his first eight years hangs on, and why Dunn moves the years before it earlier.
